messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert for tenant=acme-corp in dedicated pool=us-west-2-vpc-gpu. Symptoms: elevated 5xx on streaming endpoints, websocket disconnects ~30s. Link: https://alerts.redwood/alert/ACME-STREAM-77 :rotating_light:

Anya (on-call): taking this. Paging acme-sre (Acme Ops). I can see spike in upstream resets from the runtime: 'upstream reset by peer' across multiple hosts.

Sam L: observing same from logs — frames accepted then connection closes after ~30s. Looks like a gateway/proxy idle timeout tearing streams.

Acme Ops: yep we got customer complaints. Our app gateway (F5) has an idle timeout of 30s for streaming endpoints by default. Handshakes succeed. After ~30s no traffic for the GW and it tears the TCP.

Anya (on-call): do we see keepalives from client side? Any pings?

Sam L: client side keepalives are intermittent. The streaming protocol here relies on occasional frame traffic. If gateway drops idle TCP, upstream sees EOF.

Kevin (SRE): quick mitigation options — 1) tell acme to bump gateway timeout to 120s / enable proxy keepalive, 2) we can route acme tenant traffic through a different frontend that preserves long-lived connections, or 3) apply a proxy-level pinger from our side. Which is fastest?

Acme Ops: we can push a config change but need a maintenance window for permanent. Short-term we can flip the GW timeout but need a rollback plan in case of perf issues.

Anya (on-call): immediate plan: 1) apply emergency routing for acme to a dedicated streaming-friendly front (keeps idle alive) — Kevin please execute. 2) Ask Acme to increase gateway timeout to 120s as follow-up. 3) monitor 5xx and stream disconnect rates. Matt D will take handoff after mitigation.

Kevin (SRE): executing emergency route now. Patch to control-plane:
```
# emergency routing to bypass problematic edge
curl -X POST "https://control.redwood/api/v1/routing/emergency"
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"tenant":"acme-corp","target":"streaming-edge-v2","reason":"gateway idle timeout causing websocket resets"}'
```

deploy-bot: rollout started for route emergency/streaming-edge-v2 -> 4 hosts.

deploy-bot: rollout complete. 4/4 hosts updated.

incident-bot: Observability: 5xx rate for acme-corp decreased from 6.2% -> 0.8% in 3m after route change. Streaming disconnects trended down.

Acme Ops: we deployed a config patch to our GW to set proxy_read_timeout=120s and enabled tcp-keepalive. We'll monitor — please keep us in the loop if you still see resets. :thumbsup:

Sam L: verifying from runtime — connection lifetimes are stable, no EOFs in last 10m.

Anya (on-call): summary for handoff: Root cause: idle timeout on customer app gateway (30s) closing long-lived websocket connections; manifested as upstream resets and 5xx. Mitigation: emergency routing applied for acme-corp to streaming-edge-v2, and Acme changed GW timeout to 120s. Impact: reduced 5xx and customer streaming errors.

Matt D: taking over incident ownership. Next steps — follow up with Acme to schedule permanent route/edge config or document required gateway settings, formal postmortem, and check whether our L7 health checks/tracers can detect gateway-level idle timeouts earlier. I'll coordinate.

Acme Ops: thanks team. We'll open a change ticket and share the GW config diff once it's in prod. Appreciate the fast routing patch.

Kevin (SRE): added runbook note under dedicated-pools/tenant-isolation: 'If websocket resets with ~30s pattern, check customer-side GW idle timeout and consider emergency routing to streaming-edge-v2.'

incident-bot: SEV2 downgraded to SEV3 at 1778124120. Postmortem owner: Matt D.

Matt D: scheduling a 30min post-incident sync for tomorrow 10:00 PST. Invite will go to oncall, eng-runtime, eng-sre, and Acme Ops.

Anya (on-call): handing off until then. If anything regresses ping @Matt D and re-escalate. :white_check_mark:

Acme Ops: confirmed stable from our end for 45m. No user-facing errors since the fix.

Sam L: logs archived to /mnt/incident-logs/1778123456 for postmortem. Relevant snippets saved.

Kevin (SRE): follow-up action items added to incident ticket: [1] formalize detection for GW idle-close signature, [2] add customer onboarding checklist item about gateway timeouts for streaming, [3] consider an internal metric for sustained half-open streams.

Matt D: closing thread for now. Will attach timeline and owner notes to the incident ticket. Thanks all.
